kanji.note: Usage Tip: Use 兄 (あに) for your own brother and お兄さん (おにいさん) for someone else's. My elder brother is a junior high school teacher. ((my) elder brother: 兄) Do you have an elder brother? ((someone's) elder brother: お兄さん) How many brothers and sisters do you have? (siblings: 兄弟) 兄

Usage Tip: 兄弟 (きょうだい) combines elder and younger brother and means siblings in general. I have two younger brothers. ((my) younger brother: 弟) How old is your younger brother? ((someone's) younger brother: 弟さん) How many brothers and sisters do you have? (siblings: 兄弟) 弟

Usage Tip: Woman (女) + market (市). Use 姉 (あね) for your own sister and お姉さん for someone else's. On Sunday I went to see a movie with my elder sister. ((my) elder sister: 姉) Is your elder sister well? ((someone's) elder sister: お姉さん) My elder sister works at a bank. (elder sister: 姉) 姉

Usage Tip: Woman (女) + not yet (未) = younger sister. Add さん when it is someone else's sister. My younger sister is good at cooking. ((my) younger sister: 妹) What does your younger sister do for a living? ((someone's) younger sister: 妹さん) My younger sister is a first-year university student. (younger sister: 妹) 妹

Usage Tip: Read おや for a parent and シン for closeness: 親切 (kind), 両親 (both parents). My parents are doctors. (parent: 親) The people at that shop are very kind. (kind: 親切) I live with my parents. (parents: 両親) 親

Usage Tip: Altar (礻) on the left = ancestor. 祖父 / 祖母 are your own grandparents. I sent photos of my trip to my grandfather. (grandfather: 祖父) My grandmother is in hospital now. (grandmother: 祖母) My grandparents live in the countryside. (grandparents: 祖父・祖母) 祖

Usage Tip: Means a family or group. 家族 (family) and 水族館 (aquarium, "hall of water tribes"). I always carry a photo of my family. (family: 家族) On Sunday I went to the aquarium with my family. (aquarium: 水族館) There are four people in my family. (family: 家族) 族

Usage Tip: 主人 is "my (own) husband" or the master of a house or shop. Someone else's husband is ご主人. My husband is in America. (husband: 主人) The owner of this shop is very kind. (owner / master: 主人) I went on a trip with my husband, just the two of us. (husband: 主人) 主

Usage Tip: As a suffix ~者 is a person who does something: 医者 (doctor), 学者 (scholar). Someone from our company will call you. (person, humble: 者) When I was a child, I wanted to become a doctor. (doctor: 医者) That person is a famous scholar. (scholar: 学者) 者

Usage Tip: A suffix for a member or employee: 店員, 会社員, 銀行員, 駅員. The staff at that shop are very kind. (shop clerk: 店員) My father is an office worker. (office worker: 会社員) I asked a bank clerk how to use the ATM. (bank clerk: 銀行員) A station attendant told me how to get there. (station employee: 駅員) 員

Usage Tip: Person (亻) + root (本) = body. 体にいい means "good for your health". Who is that big person over there? (body: 体) Sport is good for your health. (good for health: 体にいい) Please take care of yourself. (take care of your health: 体に気をつける) 体

Usage Tip: 頭が痛い = headache. 頭がいい literally "good head" means clever. I had a headache, so I took the day off work. (head: 頭) My younger brother is smart. (be clever: 頭がいい) I put a hat on my head. (head: 頭) 頭
Usage Tip: Head (頁) radical on the right. 顔色が悪い means "look pale / unwell". I've forgotten that person's face. (face: 顔) I wash my face in the morning. (face: 顔) You look pale. (complexion: 顔色) 顔

Usage Tip: 首 is the neck. In 首都 (しゅと = capital city) it means "head, chief". That bird has a long neck, doesn't it? (neck: 首) My neck hurts. (neck: 首) It's cold, so I wear a scarf around my neck. (neck: 首) 首

Usage Tip: 声 is a voice of a person or animal. A sound made by a thing is 音 (おと). Excuse me, please speak in a louder voice. (voice: 声) I can hear birds singing. (voice / call: 声) Let's talk quietly. (voice: 声) 声

Usage Tip: Standalone 力 is read ちから. In compounds it is often リョク, as in 能力 (ability). Men have more strength than women. (power / strength: 力) When is this year's Japanese Language Proficiency Test? (ability: 能力) Let's work hard together. (join forces: 力を合わせる) 力

Usage Tip: Means medicine or healing. 医学 (medical science), 医者 (doctor), 医院 (clinic). I studied Western medicine at university. (medical science: 医学) When I was a child, I wanted to become a doctor. (doctor: 医者) You had better go to the doctor. (doctor: 医者) 医

Usage Tip: The radical 疒 marks illness. Key words: 病気 (illness) and 病院 (hospital). Last week I was off work because I was ill. (illness: 病気) I'm going to the hospital, so I'll leave early. (hospital: 病院) My grandmother is in hospital because she is sick. (sick: 病気) 病

Usage Tip: An institution: 病院 (hospital), 大学院 (graduate school). 入院 = enter hospital, 退院 = leave. I'm going to the hospital, so I'll leave early. (hospital: 病院) My younger sister is in hospital now. (be hospitalized: 入院する) I think my sister can leave hospital next week. (leave hospital: 退院する) 院

Usage Tip: Grass (艹) + music (楽) = medicine. In Japanese you "drink" medicine: 薬を飲む. I had a headache, so I took some medicine and went to bed. (medicine: 薬) Please take this medicine three times a day. (medicine: 薬) There is a pharmacy in front of the station. (pharmacy: 薬屋) 薬

Usage Tip: The first of the four seasons: 春 (spring), 夏 (summer), 秋 (autumn), 冬 (winter). Every year we go cherry-blossom viewing in spring. (spring: 春) I'll go back to my country during the spring break. (spring vacation: 春休み) When spring comes, it gets warm. (spring: 春) 春

Usage Tip: 夏休み (summer vacation) is the most common compound. 暑い (hot) goes with 夏. This summer I am going to Hawaii with my company. (summer: 夏) The summer holidays start next week. (summer vacation: 夏休み) Summer in Japan is very hot. (summer: 夏) 夏

Usage Tip: Grain (禾) + fire (火): the harvest season, when crops turn the colour of fire. Last autumn I went camping with friends. (autumn: 秋) I like autumn because it is cool. (autumn: 秋) In autumn the leaves turn red. (autumn: 秋) 秋

Usage Tip: The two dots at the bottom represent ice. 寒い (cold) goes with 冬. Every winter I go skiing in Canada. (winter: 冬) What will you do in the winter holidays? (winter vacation: 冬休み) It's cold in winter, isn't it? (winter: 冬) 冬

Usage Tip: 暑い is used only for hot weather. For hot things (tea, water), use 熱い, also read あつい. It's hot today, isn't it? (hot weather: 暑い) Summer in Japan is very hot. (hot: 暑い) It's hot, so please open the window. (hot: 暑い) 暑

Usage Tip: 寒い is for cold weather or air. For cold things (drinks), use 冷たい (つめたい). Is it cold outside today? (cold weather: 寒い) Hokkaido is very cold in winter. (cold: 寒い) It's cold, so please wear a coat. (cold: 寒い) 寒

Usage Tip: Alone it is かぜ (wind). Careful: 風邪 (a cold) is also read かぜ. The wind is strong today, isn't it? (wind: 風) There are many typhoons in summer. (typhoon: 台風) A cool breeze comes in through the window. (wind / breeze: 風) 風
Usage Tip: 光 (ひかり) is light. In 観光 (sightseeing) it is read コウ. The moonlight came into the room. (light: 光) The sunlight is dazzling. (light: 光) Kyoto is famous for sightseeing. (sightseeing: 観光) 光

Usage Tip: Sun (日) + moon (月) = bright. 明日 has a special reading: あした / あす. This shop is bright, isn't it? (bright: 明るい) I will go out early tomorrow morning. (tomorrow: 明日) Please explain in Japanese. (explain: 説明する) 明

Usage Tip: Sun (日) + sound (音). 暗い (dark) is the opposite of 明るい (bright). The sky has suddenly grown dark; it looks like rain. (dark: 暗い) It's dark, so please turn on the light. (dark: 暗い) In winter it gets dark around five. (become dark: 暗くなる) 暗

Usage Tip: Appears in every day of the week: 月曜日, 火曜日, 水曜日, 木曜日, 金曜日, 土曜日, 日曜日. Saturday is a day off. (Saturday: 土曜日) I go to see a movie on Sunday. (Sunday: 日曜日) What day of the week is it today? (what day: 何曜日) 曜

Usage Tip: Means "gone / past". 去年 (きょねん) is "last year", the year that has gone away. I came to Japan last summer. (last year: 去年) This year is hotter than last year. (last year: 去年) Let's forget the past. (the past: 過去) 去

Usage Tip: 早い is early in time. For speed (fast), 速い is used. Both are read はやい. "Please come at 6 a.m." "That's early!" (early: 早い) I get up early every morning. (early, adverb: 早く) Let's go to bed early today. (early: 早く) 早

Usage Tip: 遅い = late or slow (opposite of 早い / 速い). 遅れる = to be late for something (に). It's already late, so let's go home. (late: 遅い) I am a slow walker. (slow: 遅い) This morning I was ten minutes late for work. (be late: 遅れる) 遅

Usage Tip: 代わりに means "instead of". As a suffix ~代 is a fee (電気代) or an era (時代, 60年代). Mr. Nakayama will go on my behalf. (on behalf of: 代わりに) I often travelled in my student days. (time / period: 時代) I often listen to music from the 60s. (the 60s: 六十年代) This month's electricity bill was high. (charge / fee: ~代) 代

Usage Tip: お世話になっています is a set business greeting: "thank you for your continued support". Thank you for always taking care of us. (care: 世話) That is the tallest building in the world. (world: 世界) I look after the dog. (take care of: 世話をする) 世

Usage Tip: 界 means a boundary or circle of activity. Learn it as part of 世界 (world). That is the tallest building in the world. (world: 世界) Someday I want to travel all around the world. (all over the world: 世界中) There are many countries in the world. (world: 世界) 界

Usage Tip: Words (言) + ten (十) = to count or measure. 時計 has the special reading とけい. I bought this watch when I went to Hawaii. (watch / clock: 時計) What do you think about this plan? (plan: 計画) The clock is five minutes fast. (clock: 時計) 計

Usage Tip: Counts times (一度 = once) and degrees (25度). 今度 can mean "this time" or "next time". Please say it once more. (once: 一度) Shall we go for a meal next Sunday? (next time: 今度) I did well on this test. (this time: 今度) It is about 25 degrees today. (degrees: ~度) 度

Usage Tip: The shape is a circle in a circle. ~回 counts times: 一回, 二回, 何回. When you raise the lever, the motor turns. (turn / go round: 回る) I have been to that aquarium three times. (three times: 三回) I go to the pool twice a week. (twice: 二回) 回

Usage Tip: The shape is a field divided by paths. Very common in surnames: 田中, 山田, 本田. This is Mr. Yamada. (Yamada, surname: 山田) That is Mr. Tanaka over there. (Tanaka, surname: 田中) They grow rice in the paddy field. (rice field: 田んぼ) 田

Usage Tip: Two trees (木木) = a grove. Three trees (森) = a forest. Common in surnames: 小林, 林. That elementary school stands in a grove. (grove: 林) I took a walk in the woods. (woods: 林) Mr. Kobayashi is my friend. (Kobayashi, surname: 小林) 林

Usage Tip: Three trees = forest, bigger and denser than 林 (grove). Also a common surname. I stayed at a small hotel in the forest. (forest: 森) There are many birds in this forest. (forest: 森) Mr. Mori is a department head at the company. (Mori, surname: 森) 森

Usage Tip: Water (氵) radical. 池 is a pond; 電池 (でんち) means a battery. I rode a boat on the pond in the park with my child. (pond: 池) There are many fish in the pond. (pond: 池) I took photos near the pond. (pond: 池) 池

Usage Tip: Alone it is うみ (sea). Read カイ in compounds: 海外 (overseas), 海岸 (seashore). I plan to go to the sea in the summer holidays. (sea: 海) The weather was nice, so I ran along the beach with my dog. (seashore: 海岸) I want to travel abroad at New Year. (overseas: 海外) 海

Usage Tip: Water (氵) + sheep (羊). Means "ocean", and by extension "Western": 洋服, 洋食, 洋室. My elder sister has a lot of clothes. (clothes: 洋服) My younger sister likes Western food. (Western food: 洋食) I am studying Western literature. (the West: 西洋) 洋

Usage Tip: The shape shows a cow's head with horns. Read ギュウ in food words: 牛乳, 牛肉. There are lots of cows over there. (cow: 牛) I drink milk every morning. (milk: 牛乳) I bought beef at the supermarket. (beef: 牛肉) 牛

Usage Tip: A picture of a bird with its tail and feet (灬). Compare 島 (island). There are many birds in the tree. (bird: 鳥) There is a small white bird at my friend's house. (small bird: 小鳥) Let's go and eat yakitori. (grilled chicken: 焼き鳥) 鳥

Usage Tip: 大 (big) with a dot = dog. Don't confuse it with 太 (fat), which has the dot inside. When I was a child, we had a big dog at home. (dog: 犬) I walk the dog every morning. (dog: 犬) Which do you like better, dogs or cats? (dog: 犬) 犬
Usage Tip: Add an animal before 肉: 牛肉 (beef), 豚肉 (pork), 鶏肉 (chicken). I like fish better than meat. (meat: 肉) I bought beef at the supermarket. (beef: 牛肉) I like pork dishes. (pork: 豚肉) 肉

Usage Tip: Grass (艹) on top: a plant. 茶色 (tea colour) means brown; 喫茶店 (きっさてん) is a café. Won't you have some tea? (tea: お茶) I bought this old rice bowl for 30,000 yen. (rice bowl: 茶わん) I bought brown boots. (brown: 茶色) 茶

Usage Tip: Food (食) + oppose (反). ご飯 means cooked rice and also a meal: 朝ご飯, 昼ご飯, 晩ご飯. Which do you eat more often, bread or rice? (cooked rice: ご飯) Every day I study for an hour before dinner. (dinner: 夕飯) Did you eat breakfast? (breakfast: 朝ご飯) 飯

Usage Tip: Two meanings: ingredients (料理 = cooking) and fees (授業料, 無料 = free of charge). My mother is good at cooking. (cooking: 料理) How much is the tuition? (tuition: 授業料) Admission to this museum is free. (free of charge: 無料) 料

Usage Tip: 理 means reason or logic. 無理 (no reason) means "impossible" or "unreasonable". Please tell me the reason. (reason: 理由) That is impossible. (impossible: 無理) My mother is good at cooking. (cooking: 料理) 理

Usage Tip: Mouth (口) + not yet (未) = taste. 意味 (meaning) and 趣味 (hobby) use ミ. What does it taste like? (taste / flavour: 味) What does "kojichu" mean? (meaning: 意味) My mother's cooking tastes good. (taste: 味) 味

Usage Tip: Village (里) + give (予) = field. Key words: 野菜 (vegetable) and 野球 (baseball, "field ball"). That greengrocer's vegetables are cheap. (vegetable: 野菜) Let's eat vegetables every day. (vegetable: 野菜) My younger brother likes baseball. (baseball: 野球) 野

Usage Tip: Grass radical (艹) on top: a plant you pick. Learn it together with 野 in 野菜 (vegetable). That greengrocer's vegetables are cheap. (vegetable: 野菜) I made vegetable soup. (vegetable: 野菜) I like vegetables more than meat. (vegetable: 野菜) 菜

Usage Tip: 青い is an い-adjective; 青 is the noun. A "green" traffic light is called 青 in Japanese. I saw a cat with blue eyes. (blue, adjective: 青い) The traffic light turned green. (blue / green, noun: 青) The blue sky is beautiful. (blue: 青い) 青

Usage Tip: 黒い is the adjective (黒いペン); 黒 is the noun (黒が好きです). Opposite of 白. Please write with a black pen. (black, adjective: 黒い) As for colours, I like black. (black, noun: 黒) I have a black bag. (black: 黒い) 黒

Usage Tip: Colour + 色 makes colour names: 茶色 (brown), 黄色 (yellow), 水色 (light blue). I want curtains in a bright colour. (colour: 色) I bought brown boots. (brown: 茶色) What colour do you like? (what colour: 何色) 色

Usage Tip: 強い (strong) is the opposite of 弱い (weak). Read キョウ in 勉強. That person is strong. (strong: 強い) I study for more than an hour every day. (study: 勉強する) The wind is strong today. (strong: 強い) 強

Usage Tip: 弱い (weak) is the opposite of 強い (strong). ~に弱い means "bad at ~". Women are physically weaker than men. (weak: 弱い) I have a weak constitution. (weak: 弱い) My younger brother is weak at maths. (weak at: ~に弱い) 弱

Usage Tip: 重い (heavy) is the opposite of 軽い (light). It can also mean serious, as in 重い病気. This is heavy, so I can't carry it alone. (heavy: 重い) This luggage is very heavy. (heavy: 重い) He was hospitalised with a serious illness. (serious: 重い) 重

Usage Tip: 軽い (light in weight) is the opposite of 重い (heavy). Vehicle (車) radical on the left. This is light, so I can carry it by myself. (light: 軽い) Please carry the light bags. (light: 軽い) I have a light meal in the morning. (light: 軽い) 軽

Usage Tip: 大 (big) with a dot inside. 太い = thick; 太る = to put on weight (太っています = is fat). An elephant's legs are thick. (thick: 太い) I ate too much and put on weight. (gain weight: 太る) Please write with a thick pen. (thick: 太い) 太

Usage Tip: 低い (low) is the opposite of 高い (high). For a short person, use 背が低い. This table is low. (low: 低い) My younger brother is short. (short in height: 背が低い) The temperature is low today. (low: 低い) 低

Usage Tip: 短い (short in length or time) is the opposite of 長い (long). Not for height: use 低い. A one-hour lesson is short. (short: 短い) I had my hair cut short. (short: 短く) The days are short in winter. (short: 短い) 短

Usage Tip: 遠い (far) is the opposite of 近い (near). 遠く means "a distant place". My house is far from the station, so it's inconvenient. (far: 遠い) Mr. Yamada commutes to the office from far away. (distant place: 遠く) The school is not far. (far: 遠い) 遠

Usage Tip: 若い (young) is used for people and animals. For things, "new" is 新しい instead. When I was young, I often watched movies. (young: 若い) Who is that young person? (young: 若い) My grandmother looks younger than her age. (young: 若く) 若

Usage Tip: 正しい means correct. 正月 (しょうがつ) is the New Year holiday period. Is this kanji correct? (right / correct: 正しい) I go to Hawaii every New Year. (New Year: 正月) Please circle the correct answer. (correct: 正しい) 正

Usage Tip: 特に means "especially". 特急 (とっきゅう) is short for 特別急行, the limited express. This movie is especially interesting. (especially: 特に) The limited express is faster than the express. (limited express: 特急) Today is a special day. (special: 特別) 特

Usage Tip: 別れる means to part from someone. 別の means "another / different"; 別に means "separately". I broke up with my boyfriend three days ago. (part / separate: 別れる) It's raining today, so let's make it another day. (another: 別) Please put the food and drinks in separately. (separately: 別に) Today is a special day, so I bought a cake. (special: 特別) 別

Usage Tip: 便利 (convenient) and its opposite 不便 (inconvenient) are both な-adjectives. It's close to the station here, so it's convenient. (convenient: 便利) There is no electricity or water here, so it is very inconvenient. (inconvenient: 不便) Smartphones are very convenient. (convenient: 便利) 便

Usage Tip: Grain (禾) + knife (刂) = profit, benefit. 便利 (convenient) and 利用 (use). This park can be used until five in the evening. (make use of: 利用する) It's close to the station here, so it's convenient. (convenient: 便利) I often use the library. (make use of: 利用する) 利

Usage Tip: A negative prefix like "un-" or "in-": 便 (convenient) becomes 不便 (inconvenient). There is no electricity here, so it is very inconvenient. (inconvenient: 不便) I feel uneasy about living alone. (anxious: 不安) Transport in this town is inconvenient. (inconvenient: 不便) 不

Usage Tip: 心 alone is こころ. In compounds it is シン: 心配 (worry), 安心 (relief), 熱心 (eager). My father is broad-minded. (heart / mind: 心) Please don't worry. (worry: 心配) It's all right now, so please be relieved. (be relieved: 安心する) That teacher is very enthusiastic. (eager: 熱心) 心

Usage Tip: 元 means origin or source. 元気 literally means "original energy", i.e. healthy and lively. How are you? (healthy / well: 元気) The children are very lively. (lively: 元気) Please speak in a cheerful voice. (cheerful: 元気な) 元

Usage Tip: Woman (女) + child (子) = like. 好き is a な-adjective and takes が: 犬が好きです. What kind of songs do you like? (like: 好き) My wife loves shopping. (love: 大好き) What is your favourite food? (favourite: 好きな) 好

Usage Tip: 悪い (bad) is the opposite of いい / 良い (good). 目が悪い means poor eyesight. My eyesight is bad. (bad: 悪い) The weather is bad today, isn't it? (bad: 悪い) I feel unwell, so I'm going home. (feel ill: 気分が悪い) 悪

Usage Tip: A tree (木) trapped in a box (囗) = in trouble. Usually used as 困っています. I'm in trouble because I have no money. (be in trouble: 困る) If you have any problems, please tell me any time. (have trouble: 困る) I was in trouble because I didn't know the way. (be in trouble: 困る) 困

Usage Tip: 建てる (build) is transitive; 建つ (be built) is intransitive. 建物 means a building. I want to build a house in Tokyo in five years. (build: 建てる) A big building was built in front of the station. (be built: 建つ) Shinagawa has many tall buildings. (building: 建物) 建

Usage Tip: 場 alone is ば (場所). As a suffix it is ジョウ: 工場, 会場, ゴルフ場, 駐車場. I'll email you the place and time later. (place: 場所) That is a beer factory. (factory: 工場) Is there a car park near here? (car park: 駐車場) Where is the party venue? (venue / hall: 会場) 場

Usage Tip: Alone it is ところ. Compounds: 台所 (だいどころ), 住所, 近所, 事務所, 場所. What kind of place is the town where Mr. Yamada was born? (place: 所) Do you know the president's address? (address: 住所) The neighbourhood children have gathered. (neighbourhood: 近所) Please tell me how to get to the office. (office: 事務所) 所

Usage Tip: Noun + 屋 = a shop: 本屋 (bookshop), パン屋 (bakery), 花屋 (florist). 部屋 (へや) means room. I bought a newspaper at the bookshop. (~ shop: ~屋) I bought three apples at the greengrocer's. (vegetable store: 八百屋) Let's have a barbecue on the rooftop. (rooftop: 屋上) 屋

Usage Tip: A suffix for public buildings: 旅館, 大使館, 図書館, 映画館, 美術館. Please fax me a map to the Japanese inn. (Japanese inn: 旅館) That library has Japanese textbooks too. (library: 図書館) I went to a cinema in Roppongi with my younger sister. (movie theater: 映画館) Won't you go to the art museum? (art museum: 美術館) 館

Usage Tip: A large hall. 食堂 (eating hall) is a dining room, canteen or cafeteria. Every day I eat lunch in the company cafeteria. (dining hall: 食堂) The school cafeteria is cheap. (cafeteria: 食堂) The entrance ceremony is held in the auditorium. (auditorium: 講堂) 堂

Usage Tip: A suffix for rooms: 教室 (classroom), 会議室 (meeting room), 洋室 / 和室 (Western / Japanese room). The classrooms at this school are spacious and clean. (classroom: 教室) Is this meeting room free now? (meeting room: 会議室) Does that inn have Western-style rooms? (Western-style room: 洋室) 室

Usage Tip: A picture of a double gate. It is part of 開 (open), 閉 (close), 間 and 問. When I opened the gate, there was a big dog. (gate: 門) I'm waiting in front of the school gate. (gate: 門) The gate closes at six. (gate: 門) 門

Usage Tip: Means public or official. 公園 is a public garden (park). I go home through the park. (park: 公園) On Sunday I play in the park with my child. (park: 公園) There is a big park in this town. (park: 公園) 公

Usage Tip: An enclosure (囗) = garden. 公園 (park), 動物園 (zoo), 幼稚園 (kindergarten). I go home through the park. (park: 公園) I saw a baby panda at the zoo. (zoo: 動物園) My younger brother goes to kindergarten. (kindergarten: 幼稚園) 園

Usage Tip: Means "capital". 東京 is the "eastern capital"; 京都 is the old capital. Tokyo has many people and many cars. (Tokyo: 東京) I will travel to Kyoto next month. (Kyoto: 京都) Let's meet at Tokyo Station. (Tokyo Station: 東京駅) 京

Usage Tip: 都 is used for Tokyo (東京都). Japan's divisions are 都・道・府・県. I looked at the Tokyo Metropolitan Government's website. (Tokyo metropolis: 東京都) Kyoto is an old city. (Kyoto: 京都) Tokyo metropolis has 23 wards. (Tokyo metropolis: 東京都) 都

Usage Tip: The most common division of Japan: ~県. Most of Japan's 47 prefectures are 県. Globefish is famous in Yamaguchi Prefecture. (Yamaguchi Prefecture: 山口県) I live in Chiba Prefecture. (Chiba Prefecture: 千葉県) Japan has 43 prefectures (県). (prefecture: 県) 県

Usage Tip: A city ward: 目黒区, 渋谷区. 区役所 is the ward office. I live in Meguro Ward. (Meguro Ward: 目黒区) I changed my address at the ward office. (ward office: 区役所) I want to live in one of Tokyo's 23 wards. (ward: ~区) 区

Usage Tip: 市 (city) > 町 (town) > 村 (village). Also 市民 (citizen), 市役所 (city hall). There is a big library in Machida City. (Machida City: 町田市) This was a village, but it became a city last year. (city: 市) Once a month the citizens get together for a meeting. (citizen: 市民) 市

Usage Tip: Tree (木) + measure (寸) = village. The smallest of 市・町・村. This was a village, but it became a city last year. (village: 村) My grandfather lives in a small village. (village: 村) This village is quiet and beautiful. (village: 村) 村
Usage Tip: Field (田) + street (丁). 町 is a town, smaller than a city (市). I was born in a small town in California. (town: 町) This town is quiet. (town: 町) There is a big park in the town. (town: 町) 町

Usage Tip: Means people or citizens: 市民 (citizen), 国民 (nation's people), 民族 (ethnic group). Once a month the citizens get together for a meeting. (citizen: 市民) I swam at the public (city) pool. (citizen: 市民) It is a national holiday. (the people of a nation: 国民) 民

Usage Tip: Earth (土) + also (也). Read チ in 地下, 地図 and ジ in 地震 (earthquake). The meat counter is in the basement. (underground / basement: 地下) There was a big earthquake this morning. (earthquake: 地震) I go to work by subway. (subway: 地下鉄) 地

Usage Tip: Read ズ in 図 and 地図 (map), and ト in 図書館 (library). Please look at the diagram and think. (diagram / figure: 図) I went to my friend's house looking at a map. (map: 地図) I borrow books from the library. (library: 図書館) 図

Usage Tip: 服 is clothing in general. 洋服 = Western clothes; 和服 = Japanese clothes (kimono). Where did you buy those clothes? (clothes: 服) I went wearing clothes I borrowed from my sister. (Western clothes: 洋服) I'll wear new clothes to the party. (clothes: 服) 服

Usage Tip: Two meanings: 着る (wear clothes on the upper body) and 着く (arrive at a place). May I try this suit on? (put on / wear: 着る) Where is the underwear section? (underwear: 下着) What time does this train arrive in Tokyo? (arrive: 着く) 着

Usage Tip: Water (氵) + first (先). 洗う = wash; 洗濯 = laundry; お手洗い = toilet. I get up, wash my face and then eat breakfast. (wash: 洗う) I do the laundry about three times a week. (do laundry: 洗濯する) Let's wash our hands before eating. (wash: 洗う) 洗

Usage Tip: 起きる (I get up) is intransitive; 起こす (wake someone up) is transitive. What time did you get up this morning? (get up, vi.: 起きる) Please wake me up at seven. (wake somebody up, vt.: 起こす) I get up at six every morning. (get up: 起きる) 起

Usage Tip: Roof (宀) radical. 寝る = go to bed / sleep. Its opposite is 起きる (get up). I'm travelling from tomorrow, so I'll go to bed early today. (go to bed: 寝る) I go to bed at eleven every night. (go to bed: 寝る) The baby is sleeping. (sleep: 寝る) 寝

Usage Tip: Two people (人人) on the ground (土) under a roof = sit. 座る takes に: いすに座る. This chair is low and hard to sit on. (sit down: 座る) Please, have a seat. (sit down: 座る) I couldn't get a seat on the train. (sit: 座る) 座

Usage Tip: 席 is a seat. 出席 = attendance; its opposite is 欠席 (absence). Is this seat free? (seat: 席) How many people will attend today's meeting? (attend: 出席する) Let's sit in a seat near the window. (seat: 席) 席

Usage Tip: Person (亻) + scholar (士) = to serve. Most common in 仕事 (work) and 仕方がない. It can't be helped. (no help for it: 仕方がない) I have a lot of work today. (work: 仕事) My father works at a bank. (work / job: 仕事) 仕

Usage Tip: 事 is an abstract "thing / matter". Compounds: 仕事, 火事, 食事 (meal), 大事 (important). Did you know about that matter? (thing / matter: 事) I have a lot of work today. (work: 仕事) Fire! Please call 119. (fire: 火事) There is an important meeting tomorrow. (important: 大事) 事

Usage Tip: Person (亻) + move (動) = work. A kanji made in Japan. 働く takes で for the workplace. I want to work abroad. (work: 働く) My father works at a bank. (work: 働く) I work five days a week. (work: 働く) 働

Usage Tip: The shape is a carpenter's tool. Used in 工事 (construction) and 工場 (factory). When does the gas construction work start? (construction: 工事) This place is under construction now. (under construction: 工事中) My father works at a factory. (factory: 工場) 工

Usage Tip: Means work or business: 工業 (industry), 授業 (class), 卒業 (graduation), 産業 (industry). My younger sister is studying British industry. (industry: 工業) I missed class because I was sick. (class / lesson: 授業) My younger brother graduated from university last year. (graduate: 卒業する) 業

Usage Tip: Means produce or give birth: 生産 (production), 産業 (industry). お土産 (みやげ) is a souvenir. This company produces ten million cars a year. (produce: 生産する) I want to learn about Chinese society and industry. (industry: 産業) I bought souvenirs in Kyoto. (souvenir: お土産) 産

Usage Tip: Three mouths (口) stacked: many items. Read しな in 品物 and ヒン in 食料品. My elder brother lives in Shinagawa. (Shinagawa, place name: 品川) I buy groceries once a week. (groceries: 食料品) This shop has many goods. (goods: 品物) 品

Usage Tip: Verb stem + 物 = a kind of thing: 食べ物 (food), 飲み物 (drink), 買い物 (shopping). What do you want most right now? (thing / object: 物) I always do a lot of shopping when I go abroad. (shopping: 買い物) Please buy something to eat. (food: 食べ物) A whale is not a fish; it is an animal. (animal: 動物) 物

Usage Tip: 作る is used for making things, food and documents. Read サク in compounds like 作文. Cars are made here. (make / produce: 作る) I wrote a composition on Sunday night. (composition: 作文) My mother makes a lunch box every morning. (make: 作ります) 作

Usage Tip: 用 / 用事 means an errand or business. ~用 after a noun means "for ~": 子ども用 (for kids). I have something to do, so I'll go home early. (business / something to do: 用) I have an errand tomorrow. (errand: 用事) Do you have a chair for children? (for ~: ~用) 用

Usage Tip: 使う means "to use". Read シ in 大使館 (embassy), where 大使 is an ambassador. May I use this pen? (use: 使う) I went to the embassy on Saturday. (embassy: 大使館) Please teach me how to use a computer. (how to use: 使い方) 使

Usage Tip: おと is a sound made by things. For a human or animal voice, use 声 (こえ) instead. I can hear the sound of a car. (sound: 音) Japanese pronunciation is easy. (pronunciation: 発音) Every day I listen to music on the train. (music: 音楽) 音

Usage Tip: Three readings: たのしい (fun), ガク in 音楽 (music), and ラク (easy, comfortable). The party was very enjoyable. (enjoyable: 楽しい) I'm looking forward to tomorrow's date. (pleasure / look forward to: 楽しみ) Every day I listen to music on the train. (music: 音楽) This sofa is comfortable. (easy / comfortable: 楽) 楽

Usage Tip: 歌 is a song and 歌う is to sing, so 歌を歌う means "sing a song". 歌手 (かしゅ) is a singer. I sang a Japanese song at karaoke. (sing: 歌う) Have you ever heard this song? (song: 歌) My elder sister is good at singing. (song / singing: 歌) 歌

Usage Tip: Means to reflect or project an image. Most common in 映画 (movie) and 映画館 (cinema). Won't you go to see a movie on Sunday? (movie: 映画) There is a cinema near the station. (cinema: 映画館) I saw a new movie at the cinema. (cinema: 映画館) 映

Usage Tip: Read ガ for pictures (映画, 漫画) and カク for plans and strokes (計画, 画数 = stroke count). Won't you go to see a movie on Sunday? (movie: 映画) Does the president know about that plan? (plan: 計画) My hobbies are drawing and manga. (manga: 漫画) 画

Usage Tip: 写す means to copy or to photograph. Read シャ in 写真 (photograph). I took this with a digital camera. (take a photo: 写す) Next time, please show me a photo of your brothers and sisters. (photograph: 写真) May I take photos here? (photograph: 写真) 写

Usage Tip: ま adds "exactly / truly": 真ん中 (right in the middle). 写真 is "copying the truth". There are flowers in the middle of the table. (middle / centre: 真ん中) Next time, please show me a photo of your brothers and sisters. (photograph: 写真) I have family photos displayed in my room. (photograph: 写真) 真

Usage Tip: Read ブン in most words about writing and culture: 文 (sentence), 文学, 文化, 文法. Please read this sentence. (sentence: 文) I studied literature at university. (literature: 文学) Japanese culture is interesting. (culture: 文化) Japanese grammar is easy. (grammar: 文法) 文

Usage Tip: 字 is a written character or handwriting: 字がきれいです (your handwriting is neat). Do you know how to read this character? (letter: 字) Sentences in romaji are hard to read. (roman letters: ローマ字) Kanji are interesting. (Chinese character: 漢字) 字

Usage Tip: Refers to the Han dynasty of China. 漢字 literally means "Chinese characters". How do you read this kanji? (kanji: 漢字) I memorise five kanji every day. (kanji: 漢字) Studying kanji is interesting. (kanji: 漢字) 漢

Usage Tip: 英 stands for Britain: 英語 (English), 英国 (the UK), 英会話 (English conversation). Can you speak English? (English language: 英語) I go to an English conversation school once a week. (English conversation: 英会話) Our English teacher is British. (English: 英語) 英

Usage Tip: 教える is "to teach" and also "to tell": 道を教えてください (please tell me the way). My elder sister teaches English at a high school. (teach: 教える) Is this classroom free now? (classroom: 教室) Children's education is important. (education: 教育) Every Sunday I go to a nearby church. (church: 教会) 教

Usage Tip: 習う is to learn from a teacher. 予習 = study before class; 復習 = review after class. I take cooking lessons once a week. (learn: 習う) I prepare for my lessons every day. (prepare for a lesson: 予習する) There is a test next week, so I'm going to review. (review: 復習する) 習

Usage Tip: Thread (糸) radical = knead or train. Learn it as part of 練習 (practice). I want to practise casual conversation. (practise: 練習する) I practise the piano every day. (practise: 練習する) What time does football practice start? (practice: 練習) 練

Usage Tip: Almost always met in 勉強 (study): effort (勉) + strong (強) = to study hard. I study for more than an hour every day. (study: 勉強する) I study Japanese at the library. (study: 勉強) My younger brother doesn't like studying. (studying: 勉強) 勉

Usage Tip: Stone (石) = sharpen or polish. Learn it as half of 研究 (research). My elder brother does research on animals at university. (research: 研究) Please wait in the research room until three. (study room: 研究室) I am researching Japanese culture. (research: 研究する) 研

Usage Tip: Hole (穴) + nine (九): to dig deep = investigate. 研究 = "polish and dig into" a subject. My elder brother does research on animals at university. (research: 研究) Please wait in the research room until three. (study room: 研究室) What are you researching? (research: 研究する) 究

Usage Tip: Words (言) + style (式) = to test or try. Learn it in 試験 (examination). The Japanese Language Proficiency Test is in December. (examination: 試験) I have an English exam tomorrow. (exam: 試験) I review before the exam. (exam: 試験) 試

Usage Tip: Horse (馬) on the left. Learn it as the second half of 試験 (exam); also 経験 (experience). The Japanese Language Proficiency Test is in December. (examination: 試験) The exam was very difficult. (exam: 試験) I have experience working in Japan. (experience: 経験) 験

Usage Tip: At N4 level, learn it in 質問 (a question you ask). 質 itself means quality or nature. Do you have any questions? (question: 質問) May I ask the teacher a question? (ask a question: 質問する) Please answer the question. (question: 質問) 質

Usage Tip: A mouth (口) at the gate (門) = asking. 問題 is a problem or a test question. Do you have any questions? (question: 質問) There are three questions on the test. (question: 問題) If there is a problem, please email me. (problem: 問題) 問

Usage Tip: Means topic or title. Key words: 問題 (problem) and 宿題 (homework). There are three questions on the test. (question: 問題) If there is a problem, please email me. (problem: 問題) I had no time to do my homework. (homework: 宿題) 題

Usage Tip: 答える takes に: 質問に答える (answer a question). 答え is the noun "answer". Please answer my question. (answer, verb: 答える) Do you know the answer to that problem? (answer, noun: 答え) Please write the correct answer. (answer: 答え) 答

Usage Tip: Words (言) radical. 説明 (explanation) and 小説 (novel) are the key N4 words. Please explain it once more. (explain: 説明する) When I was a university student, I often read novels. (novel: 小説) The teacher explained the grammar. (explain: 説明する) 説

Usage Tip: Sound (音) over heart (心) = intention or mind. Key words: 意味, 意見, 用意, 注意. Are you ready for the trip? (preparation: 用意) If there are no opinions, we will finish here. (opinion: 意見) Please watch out for cars. (pay attention: 注意する) What does "hisashiburi" mean? (meaning: 意味) 意

Usage Tip: Water (氵) + master (主) = pour. 注意 (attention) is literally "pouring your mind" into something. I have to get an injection tomorrow. (injection: 注射) Please watch out for cars. (pay attention: 注意する) I ordered food at the restaurant. (order: 注文) 注

Usage Tip: 考える is to think something through or consider. Its noun 考え means an idea or opinion. I'll call you after thinking it over carefully. (think / consider: 考える) I have a good idea. (idea: 考え) I am thinking about my future. (be thinking: 考えている) 考

Usage Tip: Read リョ in 旅行 (travel) and 旅館 (traditional Japanese inn). I want to travel around Europe. (travel: 旅行) I ate Japanese food at a Japanese inn. (Japanese inn: 旅館) I went on a trip to Kyoto with my family. (go on a trip: 旅行に行く) 旅
Usage Tip: Heavy (重) + power (力) = move. 自動車 is literally a "self-moving vehicle". Please don't move. (move: 動く) Children like toy cars. (car: 自動車) I exercise every day. (exercise: 運動) 動

Usage Tip: 運ぶ means to carry. ウン gives 運 (luck), 運動 (exercise) and 運転 (driving). Please carry what you bought to the car. (carry: 運ぶ) I think Mr. Nakayama is a lucky person. (luck: 運) Every morning I exercise before going to work. (exercise: 運動する) 運

Usage Tip: Vehicle (車) + turn = roll. 運転 (driving), 自転車 (bicycle), 運転手 (driver). I fell over in the street and hurt my leg. (fall down: 転ぶ) I want a new bicycle. (bicycle: 自転車) Both my father and mother drive. (drive: 運転する) My elder brother works as a taxi driver. (driver: 運転手) 転

Usage Tip: 乗る takes に: 電車に乗る (get on a train). Opposite of 降りる (get off). I got in a taxi in front of the station. (get on: 乗る) What kind of transport is there from the station? (vehicle: 乗り物) I take the train every morning. (ride: 乗る) 乗

Usage Tip: Two readings: 降りる (get off a vehicle) takes を; 降る (rain / snow falls). After getting off the bus, I walk for about ten minutes. (get off: 降りる) Is it raining now? (fall, rain: 降る) It will probably snow tomorrow. (fall, snow: 降る) 降

Usage Tip: Metal (金) + lose (失). Railways run on iron, so 地下鉄 is the "underground iron (way)". Is this iron or plastic? (iron: 鉄) I go to work by subway every day. (subway: 地下鉄) Where is the subway station? (subway: 地下鉄) 鉄

Usage Tip: Thread (糸) radical. 線 is a line; train lines are ~線 (山手線), platforms are ~番線. It's dangerous, so please don't step over the line. (line: 線) Take the Yamanote Line and get off at Tamachi Station. (Yamanote Line: 山手線) Please take the train from track 3. (track: ~番線) 線

Usage Tip: 進める (move something forward, vt.) vs 進む (go forward, vi.). Movement (辶) radical. There's no time, so let's move things along quickly. (advance, vt.: 進める) Please move forward a little more. (go forward, vi.: 進む) This clock is five minutes fast. (be fast: 進む) 進

Usage Tip: 通る = to pass through; 通う = to go regularly (to school or work). I have been along this road before. (go through / pass: 通る) There are many good shops on this street. (road / street: 通り) I commute to work by car. (commute: 通う) 通

Usage Tip: 帰る means to return to where you belong (home, your country). It is a godan verb: 帰ります. Please call me when your husband gets home. (return: 帰る) I go home at six every day. (go home: 帰る) I'll go back to my country in the summer holidays. (return: 帰る) 帰

Usage Tip: 急ぐ is "to hurry". 急に means suddenly. 急行 is an express train. There's no time, so please hurry. (hurry: 急ぐ) The next train is an express bound for Shinagawa. (express: 急行) The yen suddenly rose. (suddenly: 急に) 急

Usage Tip: Means to emit or set off. Sound changes: 出 + 発 = しゅっぱつ (not しゅつはつ). Please pay attention to the pronunciation of "ra". (pronunciation: 発音) What time will you depart tomorrow? (depart: 出発する) The train departs at nine. (depart: 出発する) 発

Usage Tip: 止める (someone stops something) vs 止まる (something stops). 中止 = cancellation. Driver, please stop in front of the station. (stop, vt.: 止める) The trains stopped because of the typhoon. (stop, vi.: 止まる) Tomorrow's party is cancelled. (cancellation: 中止) 止

Usage Tip: 送る means to send things and also to see people off or drive them somewhere. I sent a fax to the company this morning. (send: 送る) I saw my friend off to the station. (see someone off: 送る) I will send photos to my mother. (send: 送る) 送

Usage Tip: 連れて行く / 連れて来る are for people and animals; for things use 持って行く / 持って来る. I took my friend to the hospital. (take someone: 連れて行く) Next time I'll bring my husband. (bring someone: 連れて来る) I take my child to the park. (take someone: 連れて行く) 連

Usage Tip: 待つ takes を for the person or thing you wait for: 友だちを待つ (wait for a friend). I waited for my friend for two hours. (wait: 待つ) Please wait a moment. (please wait: 待って) I am waiting in front of the station. (waiting: 待っている) 待
Usage Tip: Water (氵) + eternal (永). 泳ぐ has the te-form 泳いで. I swim at a sports club once a week. (swim: 泳ぐ) My child is learning swimming. (swimming: 水泳) Let's swim in the sea. (swim: 泳ぐ) 泳

Usage Tip: 持っている means "own / have". 持って行く (take) and 持って来る (bring) are very common. Do you have a car? (have: 持つ) Mr. Yamamoto is a rich person. (rich person: お金持ち) Please take an umbrella with you. (take along: 持って行く) 持
Usage Tip: Ear (耳) + hand (又) = take. 取る means take, get, or pass (an item). Please take one you like. (take: 取る) Could you pass me that salt? (pass / take: 取る) I got my driving licence. (get: 取る) 取

Usage Tip: Hand (扌) radical. 押す (push) is the opposite of 引く (pull). If you press this switch, the light comes on. (push / press: 押す) Please push the door. (push: 押す) Please don't press the button. (press: 押す) 押

Usage Tip: A bow (弓) and its string = pull. Also 風邪を引く (catch a cold) and 辞書を引く. If you pull the lever, the door opens. (pull: 引く) I look it up in the dictionary. (look up: 辞書を引く) I caught a cold. (catch a cold: 風邪を引く) 引

Usage Tip: Hand (扌) + join (合) = pick up. Opposite of 捨てる (throw away). Note the similar shape. I picked up 10,000 yen in the street. (pick up: 拾う) Let's pick up the litter. (pick up: 拾う) I caught a taxi at the station. (catch a taxi: タクシーを拾う) 拾

Usage Tip: Opposite of 拾う. Don't confuse 捨 (throw away, 11 strokes) with 拾 (pick up, 9 strokes). Please don't throw rubbish here. (throw away: 捨てる) I threw away my old clothes. (throw away: 捨てる) Please put out the rubbish on Mondays. (throw away: 捨てる) 捨

Usage Tip: 開ける takes を (someone opens it); 開く takes が (it opens). Opposite: 閉める / 閉まる. The wind is strong, so please don't open the door. (open, vt.: 開ける) What time does that shop open? (open, vi.: 開く) May I open the window? (open: 開ける) 開

Usage Tip: Opposite of 開: 閉める / 閉まる vs 開ける / 開く. A bar (才) shutting the gate (門). When night comes, please close the curtains. (close, vt.: 閉める) The doors are closing, so please be careful. (close, vi.: 閉まる) The bank closes at three. (close: 閉まる) 閉

Usage Tip: 貸す (lend) vs 借りる (borrow): the money (貝) goes out from you when you 貸す. I don't have enough money, so please lend me some. (lend: 貸す) I lent a book to my friend. (lend: 貸す) Could you lend me an umbrella? (lend: 貸す) 貸

Usage Tip: 借りる takes に or から for the lender: 友だちに借りる. Opposite of 貸す. I borrowed five million yen from the bank. (borrow: 借りる) I borrow books from the library. (borrow: 借りる) I went wearing clothes I borrowed from my sister. (borrow: 借りる) 借

Usage Tip: 売る is transitive (to sell). 売れる is intransitive (to be sold, to sell well). Where do they sell newspapers? (sell: 売る) Where is the camera counter? (sales floor: 売り場) Beer did not sell well this year. (be sold: 売れる) 売

Usage Tip: 返す is to give something back; compare 帰る (go back home), also read かえる. Did you return the books to the library? (return / give back: 返す) Please reply as soon as possible. (reply: 返事) I'll pay back the money I borrowed. (give back: 返す) 返

Usage Tip: 受ける = receive / take an exam; 受かる = pass an exam. 受付 = reception desk. I received training at my company. (receive: 受ける) I will take the Japanese Language Proficiency Test. (take an exam: 受ける) I passed the Japanese Language Proficiency Test. (pass an exam: 受かる) The reception staff at this hospital are kind. (reception: 受付) 受

Usage Tip: Birds (隹) on a tree (木) = gathering. 集める is transitive; 集まる is intransitive. I collect foreign stamps. (gather / collect, vt.: 集める) People have gathered in front of the shop. (gather, vi.: 集まる) Please gather at the station at nine tomorrow. (gather: 集まる) 集

Usage Tip: 落とす (drop something) vs 落ちる (fall). 試験に落ちる means to fail an exam. You dropped your handkerchief. (drop, vt.: 落とす) The clock fell off the TV in the earthquake. (fall, vi.: 落ちる) Leaves are falling from the trees. (fall: 落ちる) 落

Usage Tip: 消す (put out / switch off / erase) is transitive; 消える (go out / disappear) is intransitive. Please put out the fire. (put out: 消す) Shall I turn off the TV? (turn off: 消す) The wind was strong, so the fire went out. (go out: 消える) The lights in the meeting room are off. (go off: 消える) 消

Usage Tip: Lose (亡) + heart (心) = forget. 忘れる also means to leave something behind. I forgot this kanji even though I studied it. (forget: 忘れる) I left my key at home. (leave behind: 忘れる) Please don't forget your homework. (forget: 忘れる) 忘

Usage Tip: Mouth (口) on the left = call out. 呼ぶ means to call someone or to invite them. I'm going to the hospital, so please call a taxi. (call: 呼ぶ) I invited my friends to the party. (invite: 呼ぶ) Please come in when your name is called. (call: 呼ぶ) 呼

Usage Tip: 始める takes を (someone starts something). 始まる takes が (something starts by itself). I start work at nine. (start, vt.: 始める) Has the party already started? (start, vi.: 始まる) Japanese classes begin in April. (begin: 始まる) 始

Usage Tip: Opposite of 始まる. Noun form 終わり means "the end". Remember the okurigana: 終わる. The lesson has just finished. (finish / end: 終わる) I'll go on a trip at the end of August. (the end: 終わり) What time does work finish? (finish: 終わる) 終

Usage Tip: 決める (someone decides) is transitive; 決まる (it is decided) is intransitive. I haven't decided yet when to go back to my country. (decide: 決める) Has next week's schedule been decided? (be decided: 決まる) Let's decide the date of the trip. (decide: 決める) 決

Usage Tip: 変える (vt.) / 変わる (vi.) = change. 変な = strange; 大変 = tough, or "very". I changed the colour of the curtains in my room. (change, vt.: 変える) The venue of the party has changed. (change, vi.: 変わる) That person is wearing strange clothes. (odd / strange: 変) I have a lot of work today, so it's tough. (hard / serious: 大変) 変

Usage Tip: 残す (leave something) vs 残る (be left). 残念 = what a pity; 残業 = overtime work. Please eat it all without leaving any. (leave: 残す) A lot of food was left over. (remain / be left: 残る) That's a pity. (unfortunate: 残念) I have to work overtime again today. (work overtime: 残業する) 残

Usage Tip: Thread (糸) radical. 続ける (vt.) / 続く (vi.). Verb stem + 続ける = keep doing. I want to continue studying Japanese even after the exam. (continue, vt.: 続ける) The meeting went on until night. (continue, vi.: 続く) It has been raining for three days in a row. (continue: 続く) 続

Usage Tip: Words (言) radical. 調べる means to look something up, check or investigate. Please look up the location on the internet. (investigate / check: 調べる) I look up words I don't know in the dictionary. (look up: 調べる) I checked the train times. (check: 調べる) 調

Usage Tip: 伝える is to pass on a message. 手伝う (てつだう) means to help with a task. Please tell the manager the time of tomorrow's meeting. (tell / inform: 伝える) May I leave a message? (message: 伝言) I have a lot of work today, so could you help me? (help: 手伝う) 伝

Usage Tip: 死ぬ is the only common verb ending in ぬ. Its te-form is 死んで. Last year my pet bird died. (die: 死ぬ) My grandfather died ten years ago. (die: 死ぬ) That flower died because it had no water. (die: 死ぬ) 死

Usage Tip: Verb stem + 方 means "how to": 読み方, 書き方, 使い方. Read ほう for a direction or side. Do you know this person? (person, polite: 方) Please teach me how to write it. (way of ~: ~方) I will call you at five tomorrow evening. (evening: 夕方) Please go to the right side. (direction / side: 方) 方

Usage Tip: Used as a prefix of range: 以上 (or more), 以下 (or less), 以内 (within), 以外 (except). I have time except for Friday. (except: 以外) Please write a composition within 1,000 characters. (within: 以内) I waited 30 minutes or more. (or more: 以上) It is 1,000 yen for children aged 12 or under. (or less: 以下) 以

Usage Tip: Means inside. 以内 (within), 国内 (domestic), 家内 ("inside the house" = my wife). I think Mr. Tanaka will come within five minutes. (within: 以内) Overseas trips are expensive, so let's travel domestically. (domestic: 国内) My wife is a good driver. ((my) wife: 家内) 内

Usage Tip: Means all or whole: 全部 (all), 全員 (all members), 安全 (safe), 全然 (not at all). Everyone at my company can speak English. (all the members: 全員) Do you think Japan is a safe country? (safe: 安全) I read this whole book. (all: 全部) 全

Usage Tip: Means "self". 自分 (oneself), 自動車 (automobile), 自転車 (bicycle, "self-turning vehicle"). I bought this watch myself. (oneself: 自分) I bought a toy car for my child. (car: 自動車) I go to school by bicycle. (bicycle: 自転車) 自

Usage Tip: 合う = to fit or match. 間に合う = be in time. Special readings: 場合 (ばあい), 試合 (しあい). These clothes and these shoes go well together. (fit / match: 合う) I may not make it in time for the departure. (be in time: 間に合う) If you can't go, please call. (case: 場合) There is a football match on Sunday. (match / game: 試合) 合

Usage Tip: 切る is "to cut". Read セツ in 親切 (kind) and 大切 (important). I cut my hand while cooking. (cut: 切る) I want to send a letter, so please buy some stamps. (stamp: 切手) The people at that shop are very kind. (kind: 親切) It is important to study every day. (important: 大切) 切

Usage Tip: ~台 counts cars, computers and other machines: 一台, 二台, 三台. I have two cars. (counter for machines: ~台) My mother is cooking in the kitchen now. (kitchen: 台所) A typhoon is coming next week. (typhoon: 台風) 台

Usage Tip: A part or department: 全部, 部長, 学部. ~部 counts copies. 部屋 is read へや. I read this whole book. (all: 全部) I had dinner with the department head. (department head: 部長) Please make twenty copies of this. (copies: ~部) My house has four rooms. (room: 部屋) 部

Usage Tip: 同じ is followed directly by a noun without な: 同じ本 (the same book). My car is the same as Mr. Tanaka's. (same: 同じ) We work at the same company. (same: 同じ) I play with friends from the same class. (same class: 同じクラス) 同
